scope: Owned native Rust scalar/procedure executor for lexical EPS code; not a full PostScript interpreter or EPS renderer

state.dictionary: one user dictionary plus supported system values/operators; bounded open-addressing table
state.operand_and_execution_stacks: preallocated managed buffers; no recursive Rust calls
state.procedure_identity: nonempty lexical literals retain identity; empty procedures share canonical identity, independently checked
state.integer_model: signed32; arithmetic overflow promotes exact wide integer result to f32
state.comparison: mixed equality uses real promotion; ordered comparisons preserve integer value, matching qualified independent cases
state.unsupported: strings, arrays, full dictionary stack, bind, immediate names, stream/image data and graphics; never silently ignored

limits: work ticks for instructions, name hashing/probes and bulk stack operations

ownership.all_vm_buffers: admitted to MemoryBudget before execution; failed admissions and errors release acquired storage
ownership.result: SharedBuffer retains full configured operand capacity through last owner
ownership.source_and_program: caller-owned source and managed borrowed instruction tape; procedure results are diagnostic ranges, not standalone objects

independent.role: test-only; ephemeral container, no production linkage
independent.numeric_model: Ghostscript default 64-bit integers; these cases do not require integer-overflow promotion

native_controls: 3000 operator-exec tail chain with one execution frame
dictionary, operand, frame and work limits
shared-root admission refusal and last-owner release

oracle_driven_corrections: mixed integer/real equality at f32 precision boundary
ordered comparison kept distinct from equality conversion
canonical empty procedure identity; distinct nonempty literals still compare unequal
remaining: full object VM and dictionary scopes
native graphics, paths, clipping, images and fonts
viewer cache, prefetch, swap and GPU integration
performance: No throughput/latency claim; all configured limits are resource bounds
